City Council
AGENDA
A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
June 17, 2013
7:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers
24300 Narbonne Avenue
1.
OPENING CEREMONIES
a.
Call Meeting to Order
b.
Flag Salute
c.
Invocation - Councilmember Traina
d.
Roll Call
2.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA
3.
CITY MANAGER'S REPORT
4.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY COUNCIL The City Council may discuss and act upon items described under Council Comments; however, items which are not will be limited to Council reports, announcements, or requests for clarification, or factual information, or to placement of matters on the agenda for a future meeting.
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS Persons wishing to speak on Consent Agenda items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a 5 minute time limit per person has been established. Amendments to Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibit the Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
6.
CONSENT AGENDA
All items under the Consent Agenda are considered by the Council to be routine and will be enacted by one motion in the form listed below. There may be separate discussions of these items prior to the time the Council votes on the motion. Specific items may be removed from the Consent Agenda at the request of any Councilmember or staff.
a.
Motion to Waive Further Reading
b.
Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held on June 3, 2013, the Regular City Council Meeting held on June 3, 2013, the Special City Council meeting held on May 22, 2013, and the Special City Council meeting held on June 5, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
06/03/2013 -Minutes Special Meeting
06/03/2013 -Minutes Regular Meeting
05/22/2013 -Minutes Special Meeting
06/05/2013 -Minutes Special Meeting
c.
Approval of Demands
Staff Report- item 6.C
d.
Approval of an Ordinance adding Section 11-1.70.16 (A) 1 to the Lomita Municipal Code establishing a procedure for a majority of the City Council to appeal a Planning Commission decision and changing the appeal period from 15 days to 30 days. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 6.D
e.
Award of Contract for Engineering Services for Design of the Bus Bench and Trash Container Reposition Project Using Transportation Development Act (TDA) Program Funds in the amount of $34,870. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 6.E
f.
Approval of an Amendment to the Employment Agreement with City Manager Rock. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 6.F
PUBLIC HEARINGS
7.
OVERSIZED VEHICLE ORDINANCE, discussion and consideration of an Ordinance adding Article 3 (Overnight Parking of Oversized Vehicles and Trailers) to Title VIII, Chapter 1 of the Lomita Municipal Code to add requirements for the parking of oversized vehicles and trailers, establishing a permit process and provide direction on rates for permit fees and fines.
Presented by Community Services Director McPherron.
Staff Report- item 7
8.
VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP NO. 71769, a request to allow the subdivision of a 41,849 square foot lot for sixteen new townhouse units located at 26035 Cypress Street in the RVD-2500 (Residential Variable Density) Zone. Filed by Storm Western Development of 23223 Normandie Avenue, Torrance, CA 90501.
Presented by Principal Planner Velasco.
Staff Report- item 8
9.
ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2013-05/INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE Discussion and consideration of an Ordinance amending various sections of the Lomita Municipal Code establishing definitions, designating use, and adopting planning and approval requirements for emergency shelters, transitional and supportive housing, and single room occupancy units.
Presented by Principal Planner Velasco.
Staff Report- item 9
SCHEDULED ITEMS:
10.
NOTICE OF INTENT TO PREPARE AN INDIVIDUAL WATERSHED MANAGEMENT PLAN (WMP) Pursuant to the MS4 Permit adopted by the Los Angeles County Regional Water Quality Control Board in November of 2012, the City Council will discuss and possibly consider submittal of a Notice of Intent to prepare an Individual Watershed Management Plan (WMP) to the Los Angeles Regional Water Quality Control Board (LARWQCB).
Presented by Public Works Director Damasse.
Staff Report- item 10
ADJOURNMENT
Written materials distributed to the City Council within 72 hours of the City Council meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution in the City Clerk's office at 24300 Narbonne Avenue.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, you should contact the office of the City Clerk at 310 325-7110 (voice) or the California Relay Service. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility to this meeting.
minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
June 17, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Monday, June
17, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Sanchez led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were Assistant City
Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Public Works Director Damasse, Community Services
Director McPherron, Administrative Services Director Chavez, Parks and Recreation Director
Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Savidan seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina requested a future agenda item regarding the operations and costs
associated with the Cypress Water Production Facility (CWPF). According to Councilmember
Traina, the costs for purchasing MWD Water in the FY 2012-13 budget is $119,107 less than the
budgeted amount for CWPF operations, as stated in the budget for FY 2013-14; in the FY2013-
14 budget, associated CWPF operational costs include: the new Water Treatment Operator
position (salary and benefits); the purchase of Metropolitan Water; other staff salary allocations
associated with operations; the purchase of chemicals; contract costs, such as SCADA; and
other operating expenses. Councilmember Traina stated there is no need to spend more money
for lower quality blended water, when MWD Water is both cheaper and of better quality.
Councilmember Traina added that maybe in future years rate payers might see some savings
from the blending of water, but not this fiscal year. Again, Councilmember Traina requested to
have a meeting to further discuss this matter in order to see what direction the City Council
would like to go regarding water blending, and to gather more input from the public. No other

  Page 1
 Councilmembers supported Councilmember Traina’s request to place this on a future agenda
for discussion.

Councilmember Sanchez stated that the cost of MWD Water in FY 2012-13 is different than that
budgeted in FY 2013-14, which is due to the increase in the City’s cost to purchase MWD
Water. According to Councilmember Sanchez, the actual budgeted cost for purchasing MWD
Water this fiscal year would be around $2.56 million, if water blending were not in place.
Councilmember Sanchez also stated that the numbers being used by Councilmember Traina
were not correct.

Councilmember Traina stated that he had received another complaint from a resident regarding
calcium deposits in their pool, and that the repairs associated with such deposits were very
expensive.

Councilmember Gazeley invited Council to attend the upcoming Metro meeting on June 20,
2013, and show their opposition to the decision to allocate Measure R Funds to the
Crenshaw/LAX Transit Corridor, instead of the South Bay Highway Program Fund, as the
decision might affect Lomita.

Councilmember Gazeley stated that there was recently an incident of a person drawing a loaded
gun; Councilmember Gazeley applauded Deputy Gazeley for how the incident was handled, and
thanked the Sheriff’s Department personnel for their sacrifices and for a job well done.

Councilmember Savidan encouraged residents to give blended water a chance, and to not
come to a conclusion after only two months of CWPF operations. Furthermore, Councilmember
Savidan stated that the City’s goal is to provide quality water to residents.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, informed those in attendance that his neighbor had some repairs
done to a sink because of calcium deposits. Mr. McGrath also stated that he was opposed to
the $7,600 increase to City Manager Rock’s contract, and urged the City Council to vote “no” on
the item, as the current compensation of $160,000 is very generous for the City Manager
position in Lomita.

George Kivett, Executive Director of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, invited those in
attendance to the Chamber’s next Business Networking Mixer, which will take place at Summer
Studio’s Academy on June 27, 2013, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. Mr. Kivett also thanked
Council for their participation in, and support of, Chamber events.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, asked Council not to approve Item 7.D, which pertains to the
appeal of Planning Commission decisions, as it will make the associated processes more costly
for businesses and developers in Lomita by increasing approval timeframes. Mr. Kivett also
urged Council to shut down Well #5, and to use it only for emergency purposes. Lastly, Mr.
Kivett agreed that the proposed raise for the City Manager was too high.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, stated that previously approved contributions to two community
organizations were not fair to other community organizations in Lomita.

  Page 2
 Sharon Houston, Lomita resident, stated that for the past two months her family has had issues
with their water smelling like sulfur. Ms. Houston urged Council to once again discuss water
blending in Lomita.

Dave Albert, Lomita resident, stated that the public records request he submitted regarding the
water pumping logs and chemical usage at CWPF had not been provided to him in full.
Referring to the Lomita Continued Annual Disclosure Report, Mr. Albert noted that over the past
five years the City has lost millions of dollars in net revenues, as the City is focused on the well,
which in turn is costly for the City.

6. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Savidan
seconded the motion. Councilmember Traina asked to pull Item 7.F., and stated that he could
not support the 4.5% increase in the City Manager’s contract, as it is very excessive. The
motion to approve the Consent Agenda carried unanimously, with Councilmember Traina voting
NO on Item 7.F.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held on
  June 3, 2013, the Regular City Council Meeting held on June 3, 2013, the Special City
  Council meeting held on May 22, 2013, and the Special City Council meeting held on June
  5, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  d. Approval of an Ordinance adding Section 11-1.70.16 (A) 1 to the Lomita Municipal Code,
  establishing a procedure for a majority of the City Council to appeal a Planning
  Commission decision, and changing the appeal period from 15 days to 30 days.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  e. Award of Contract for Engineering Services for the Design of the Bus Bench and Trash
  Container Reposition Project using Transportation Development Act (TDA) Program Funds
  in the amount of $34,870. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  f. Approval of an Amendment to the Employment Agreement with City Manager Rock.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6. OVERSIZED VEHICLE ORDINANCE

Community Services Director McPherron provided a PowerPoint presentation (Attachment A),
and informed those in attendance that City Council and the Public Safety and Traffic
Commission had previously convened a joint meeting to discuss the proposed oversized
vehicle ordinance. According to Director McPherron, the Public Safety and Traffic Commission
recommended Option B, which is as follows: oversized vehicle and trailer permits are required
between 2 a.m. and 6 p.m., during which time owners of such vehicles could be cited without

  Page 3
 permits; the cost of a three day permit is $7; the maximum number of days an oversized vehicle
may be permitted for is 60; and weekends and City-recognized holidays would be exempt from
permit requirements. Director McPherron added that permits could be issued and obtained
online, and further noted that detached trailers are always citable, as well as any other vehicles
that exceed the established three dimension criteria. Lastly, Director McPherron stated that
should Council approve the first reading of the ordinance, a resolution to approve the fee rate
and establish fines for violations would be presented with the ordinance at the second reading.

Discussion followed regarding the registration fee, the times when citations could be issued, and
the days exempt from permit requirements.

Mayor Estrada opened the Public Hearing.

Traffic and Safety Commissioner John Carmody asked Council to approve the proposed
ordinance in order to put the City of Lomita on par with neighboring cities.

Mayor Estrada closed the Public Hearing.

Councilmember Savidan moved to adopt the first reading of the proposed ordinance with one
change, not exempting weekends (Friday, Saturday, and Sunday) from permit requirements.
Mayor Estrada seconded the motion.

Roll Call:
AYES: Mayor Estrada and Councilmember Savidan
NOES: Councilmembers Traina, Sanchez, and Gazeley
Motion Failed.

Councilmember Sanchez made a motion to increase the total amount of permit days from 60 to
90, and keeping weekends exempt from permit requirements. The motion failed for a lack of a
second.

Councilmember Traina made a motion to approve the ordinance as recommended by the Public
Safety and Traffic Commission. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried
unanimously.

7. VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP NO. 71769

Principal Planner Velasco provided a PowerPoint presentation (Attachment B). Ms. Velasco
stated that the proposed development of 16 townhouse units is a medium density residential
development, with one unit per 2,500 square feet of lot size. According to Ms. Velasco, on
March 27, 2013, Los Angeles County reviewed the proposed tentative map and did not place
any holds on the proposed map. Ms. Velasco recommended that City Council approve the

  Page 4
 tentative map.

Councilmember Traina asked whether the developer could widen the proposed street, and
discussion followed. Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that Council could condition the
development by adding that the private drive off of Cypress Street shall not have a gate or other
obstructions that would prevent vehicles from being able to turn-around or make a three point
turn.

Councilmember Sanchez made a motion to approve Item #7 per staff’s recommendation, but
with the condition that no gates or other obstructions are placed at the private drive off of
Cypress Street. Councilmember Traina seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

8. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2013-05/INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE

Principal Planner Velasco provided a PowerPoint presentation (Attachment C). Ms. Velasco
stated that Senate Bill 2, passed by the State Legislature in 2007, requires cities to remove
governmental constraints relative to special needs housing, or their Housing Elements will not
be certified. Ms. Velasco added that staff is currently in the process of preparing the City’s 2014
Housing Element, which must be submitted to HCD by October 2013.

According to Ms. Velasco, State law allows for operational standards, but limits cities on what
they can impose on emergency shelters. Therefore, Ms. Velasco stated that staff has reviewed
all requirements and other cities standards that have been successful in the past with striking a
balance between local permitting control and not placing extensive governmental constraints on
housing. Ms. Velasco stated that staff has prepared 15 operational standards for emergency
shelters, including minimum living space requirements, and a parking ratio of one space per
every 10 beds, plus one parking space per employee. According to Ms. Velasco, single room
occupancy will be allowed with a conditional use permit within the RVD zones and mixed-use
overlay zone, while transitional and supportive housing will be allowed in all residential zones
subject to all residential zoning requirements.

Councilmembers Sanchez and Traina expressed their concern that the parking requirements
were very low, and recommended two parking spaces per every 10 beds. Ms. Velasco, along
with the City’s Housing Consultant, Veronica Tam, cautioned Council that the standards are
becoming very restrictive and such changes could result in the Housing Element not being
approved. Discussion followed. Ms. Tam stated that the chance of the City of Lomita getting an
emergency shelter is almost zero, and that the proposed one parking space per every 10 beds
is typical of other city ordinances.

Mayor Estrada opened the Public Hearing.

Lomita residents, George Kivett, and Sharon Houston, agreed that the parking requirement
should be increase to two parking spaces per every 10 beds.

  Page 5
 Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, stated that the City needs to prepare detailed guidelines
regarding what has to be included in the operational standards.

Mayor Estrada closed the Public Hearing.

Councilmember Traina moved to approve Item #8 as recommended by staff, with the exception
of changing the proposed parking requirements to two spaces per every 10 beds.
Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  SCHEDULED ITEMS:

9. NOTICE OF INTENT TO PREPARE AN INDIVIDUAL WATERSHED MANAGEMENT PLAN
  (WMP)

Public Works Director Damasse stated that the City of Lomita is now subject to the MS4 Permit,
which requires that a Notice of Intent be filed with the Los Angeles Regional Water Quality
Control Board committing the City to either an Enhanced Watershed Management Plan or an
Individual Watershed Management Plan in order to meet Machado Lake TMDLs and other
requirements associated with Municipal Separate Storm Drain Systems.52

Mr. Tahir, MPDS Environmental Consultant, explained that the Enhanced Watershed
Management Plan is very costly. According to Mr. Tahir, the other option, the Individual
Watershed Management Plan, does not assure compliance through the construction of multi-
beneficial regional projects, but does allow cities to achieve compliance through a rigorous
monitoring plan and implementation of best management practices to address the critical issues
of trash, nutrients, and toxins. Mr. Tahir recommended that City Council select the Individual
Watershed Management Plan, as the best and least expensive option, which will cost the City
between $15,000 to $20,000. Mr. Tahir did however caution Council that if monitoring shows
that TMDLs are exceeding thresholds, then the City would be out of compliance immediately.

In response to Councilmember Traina’s question on whether storm drain screens would be a
potential problem as it pertains to potential flooding, Mr. Tahir responded that such screens are
retractable and should not cause a flooding problem; Mr. Tahir did state that proper maintenance
of such screens would be important.

Councilmember Traina moved to approve Item #9 as recommended by staff. Councilmember
Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 9:00 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
